newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani vegoil prices seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani vegoil prices seen firm.

text.p: Pakistani vegetable oil prices are expected to remain firm in the week started Saturday on demand from oil processing mills, dealers said.
They said Pakistan was likely to place fresh buying orders of Malaysia-origin vegoil within the next few days as local vegoil stocks had slipped in the week ended Friday.

"The local cotton seed supply is good, but mill owners from Karachi prefer Malaysian vegoil which costs less compared to local seeds brought from the Punjab province," dealer Saulat Khan said. "Pakistan is likely to place buying orders of 10,000 tonnes to 15,000 tonnes of vegeoil in the near term." He said the state-run Ghee Corporation of Pakistan (GCP) would also be a buyer in the near term.

Dealers said vegoil stocks slipped to 156,000 tonnes Friday from 175,000 tonnes a week back. RBD palm oil and palm olein stocks fell to 125,000 tonnes compared to 137,000 tonnes. Soyoil and Sunflower oil stocks rose to 24,000 from 19,000 tonnes. The GCP has a stock of 7,000 tonnes of palm oil and palm olien compared to 10,000 tonnes last week. It had booked 9,000 tonnes of RBD palm oil and palm olein for shipment by October 10.

Ship Wawasan Murni was discharging 19,000 tonnes of palm oil at Port Qasim and Bunga Angri 12,500 tonnes palm oil at Karachi. One dealer said Strength with 5,500 tonnes of palm oil was on the outer anchorage. Juliana with 6,000 tonnes of tallow is expected to arrive on Sunday and Wawasan Megah with 20,000 tonnes of palm oil on October 4. Novomir-Two is loading 15,000 tonnes of soyoil at a South American port.
